decisions.summary: A margin under the bar is used only when no wind-facing margin exists; recorded as meta.seat_offwind; forbidden on every pool map by the pool test.
decisions.why: Unchanged ruling. With the strike-out retired, the only things left that refuse every wind-facing margin are the seat's hard constraints (drain, wet toe), which FR-010 keeps and the record supports. Where they refuse every such margin, the literal rule is physically impossible, and the only alternative, renaming the wind, is the behavior the GM asked to end. The fallback never renames the wind, is recorded on the map, and is forbidden on the pool, so FR-004's pool clause holds. The debt from the previous review is paid: T21 records the count on the amended engine, 3 of 48 cohort seeds off-wind. The GM gets that number in the hand-off.

decisions.summary: brook_fords every 160 ft where the brook bends under 20 degrees; a 30 ft corridor gap each side of each ford; the spur routed through a ford; bridges() decks every crossing; far_bank, the strike-out and the brook re-roll deleted.

decisions.summary: The route lattice charges BROOK_CROSSING_COST_FT (150 ft, a guess recorded in water/270) for entering the brook's band, and the string-pull may not undo a crossing the lattice avoided (Kashikawa's lane crossed and recrossed to reach a house on its own bank). The band is kept as brook points in a 20 px bucket grid.
decisions.why: FR-011 says a way MUST be able to cross 'where the layout needs it'. A price keeps crossings available and takes away only the needless ones, like R9's cross-and-back lane. Nothing is refused: a way that has to cross still crosses when every other route costs more. No household, field path or seat loses anything FR-012 guarantees. It is a defect fix on the maps this feature re-rolled (US6, constitution XIV). The 150 ft is a guess, and the plan says so.

decisions.summary: stage_crossings squares every crossing more than 10 degrees off square (square_crossings), in the record and the ink together, before bridges() lays the deck.
decisions.why: FR-011 requires every way to cross the brook 'squarely'. R9 records a crossing 52 degrees off square before the fix and 0 after, so the decision enforces the requirement itself. The 10-degree tolerance is calibration of 'squarely', not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Where the connector hands over to the lanes, that junction is the entrance anchor. departure_routes walks every dwelling's way out through the lanes to the handover and out along the connector. Both placers keep first the seats the fewest routes miss (routes_missed, 20 ft), then those within KOSATSUBA_HANDOVER_BAND_FT (20 ft) of the handover, and the connector is offered as a way to post on. The census counts ways out that pass an entrance board. A connector that meets no other way keeps the first-arrival walk.
decisions.why: FR-015 says, word for word, 'on the way the connector meets, within the entrance band - so every departure passes it'. The handover is the one point every departure passes, so this decision puts FR-015's own purpose into code rather than a proxy for it. 'Fewest missed' ranks the seats. It does not excuse a board that some routes miss: test_pool_261 asserts routes_missed == 0 on every entrance map. I checked the one possible silent exclusion, departure_routes skipping a dwelling more than 150 px from any lane. It routes every household on all five maps (15/15, 20/20, 16/16, 12/12, 19/19). The first-arrival case is a connector with no other way to meet: there the connector is the only way, so FR-015's anchor clause has no junction to name. The census change serves FR-018, since the notes now state what the board is sited for.

The spec's own Decisions row carries the same carve-out, and the earlier measurement found nothing thin hidden in the exempted bins.

decisions.summary: The spur's origin stops on the houses' bank, short of a stream it would cross; the spur is scored against the brook gapped at the fords; trim_lane_stubs leaves the spur to the sweeps that record a drop; the dangling-ends sweep counts the dry hem, as well as the paddy, as the field.
decisions.why: FR-012 ('at least one way reaches the field') and SC-008 ('every hamlet whose field is across the brook has a way that reaches it'). Each of the three fixes removes something that stopped the engine from drawing the crossing the GM's ruling asks for: fix the algorithm, not the seat. On the dry hem: the hem plots are worked ground of the same field (the spec's Edge Case names them as cropland beside 'the crop'), and a path ending at the field's cultivated hem has reached the field on a plain reading. test_pool_261 test_a_way_reaches_the_field holds a way within 60 ft of the paddy or the hem on every map whose field lies across the brook. Wording nit: the plan says each of the three maps gets 'its one way to the rice', but Mizuguchi's spur stops at the hem, which the code comment puts 108 ft from the paddy outline. 'To the field' is the accurate phrase.

decisions.summary: ford_crossing, path_violations (the brook term and the twice-bridged count) and the first square_crossings used seg_intersect (a line test) as a segment-crossing test; each now tests segments_cross first; the connector bearings changed on four maps, and the notes' district directions were re-read from the drawn tracks.
decisions.why: A constitution XIV defect fix found in this work. It narrows nothing: it removes false crossings that pushed every spur to a ford and scored violations on connectors. The re-read district directions serve FR-018.

The test only fails when the ruled run is present, so it enforces the request rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: A non-round cluster shape is recorded as honored only past round's aspect ceiling (2.0). Inashiro's rolled crescent, drawn at 1.97, is now recorded meta.cluster_shape_unhonored.
decisions.why: FR-018: declarations must match what the map draws. Inashiro's manifest claimed a crescent that the map draws as a round cloud, and the recording mechanism for an unhonored rolled shape already existed (Kashikawa since 2026-08-16). The decision closes the 1.9-2.0 overlap that let a round drawing claim to be a crescent. It is not the route-around the GM forbade: no seed, seat or declaration was changed to dodge the engine, and the shape is a rolled knob that the spec never required a map to honor. Hand-off point for the GM, not a block: before this feature Inashiro, the reference hamlet, drew its crescent honored (notes: drawn aspect 2.49-3.25). At the new wind-facing seat it draws a round cloud, and the pool now honors a non-round shape on no map (manifests: Inashiro, Kashikawa, Mizuguchi and Sawada unhonored, Kuwabata round). Whether the placer should be made to draw the rolled shape at a wind-facing seat is the GM's 'fix the placement algorithm' question, and they should see it.
